definitions.definition: The remains of something that has been severely damaged or worn down.
An event in which something is damaged through collision.
(transitive) To destroy violently; to cause severe damage to something, to a point where it no longer works, or is useless.
definitions.example: He wrecked the car in a collision.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To ruin or dilapidate.
(transitive, obsolete) To plunder goods from wrecked ships.
(transitive) To pull or twist violently.
(transitive) To obtain by pulling or violent force.
definitions.example: He wrested the remote control from my grasp and changed the channel.

definitions.definition: (transitive, figuratively) To seize.
The act of wresting; a wrench or twist; distortion.
(music) A key to tune a stringed instrument.
(obsolete) Active or motive power.
Often followed by out: to squeeze or twist (something moist) tightly so that liquid is forced out.
definitions.example: I didn’t have a towel so I just wrung my hair dry.

definitions.definition: Often followed by from or out: to extract (a liquid) from something wet by squeezing, twisting, or otherwise putting pressure on it.
definitions.example: Put the berries into a cheesecloth and wring the juice into a bowl.

definitions.definition: To hold (someone or something) tightly and press or twist; to wrest.
definitions.example: to wring someone’s hand

definitions.definition: (also figuratively) A powerful squeezing or twisting action.
definitions.example: I grasped his hand and gave it a grateful wring.

definitions.definition: (dated) Followed by down: the product of wringing, such as cider or wine.
(obsolete) A sharp physical pain, especially in the abdomen; also, mental pain or distress.
(anatomy) The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
definitions.example: With a flick of the wrist, he threw the frisbee to a team-mate.

definitions.definition: (engineering) A stud or pin which forms a journal.
(ice hockey) To hit a wrist shot.
(ambitransitive) To form letters, words or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.
definitions.example: The pupil wrote his name on the paper.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To be the author of (a book, article, poem, etc.).
definitions.example: My uncle writes newspaper articles for The Herald.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To compose and send written information (to).
definitions.example: Please write to me when you get there.

definitions.definition: The act or style of writing.
(computing) The operation of storing data, as in memory or onto disk.
definitions.example: How many writes per second can this hard disk handle?

definitions.definition: Incorrect or untrue.
definitions.example: Some of your answers were correct, and some were wrong.

definitions.definition: Asserting something incorrect or untrue.
definitions.example: You're wrong: he's not Superman at all.

definitions.definition: Immoral, not good, bad.
definitions.example: It is wrong to lie.

definitions.definition: (informal) In a way that isn't right; incorrectly, wrongly.
definitions.example: I spelled several names wrong in my address book.

definitions.definition: Something that is immoral or not good.
definitions.example: Injustice is a heinous wrong.

definitions.definition: An instance of wronging someone (sometimes with possessive to indicate the wrongdoer).
The incorrect or unjust position or opinion.
To treat unjustly; to injure or harm; to do wrong by.
definitions.example: The dealer wronged us by selling us this lemon of a car.

definitions.definition: To deprive of some right, or to withhold some act of justice.
To slander; to impute evil to unjustly.
simple past of write
definitions.example: We all wrote down the instructions.

definitions.definition: (now colloquial and nonstandard) past participle of write
simple past and past participle of wring
definitions.example: I wrung out my wet jeans and hung them out to dry.

definitions.definition: In a wry or sarcastic manner; ironically.
Of a facial expression, contortedly.
(nautical) A slick and light ship for making pleasure trips or racing on water, having sails but often motor-powered. At times used as a residence offshore on a dock.
definitions.example: Would you like to go sailing on my uncle’s yacht?

definitions.definition: Any vessel used for private, noncommercial purposes.
(intransitive) To sail, voyage, or race in a yacht.
(intransitive, also figuratively) To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.
definitions.example: All I yearn for is a simple life.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) Of music, words, etc.: to express strong desire or longing.
(intransitive, dated) To have strong feelings of affection, love, sympathy, etc., toward someone.
A strong desire or longing; a yearning, a yen.
An often humid, yellowish froth produced by fermenting malt worts, and used to brew beer, leaven bread, and also used in certain medicines.
A single-celled fungus of a wide variety of taxonomic families.
(figuratively) A frothy foam.
To ferment.
(of something prepared with a yeasted dough) To rise.
(African-American Vernacular, slang) To exaggerate.
To give as a result or outcome; to produce or render.
definitions.example: This method generally yields better results.

definitions.definition: To give up; to surrender or capitulate.
A product.
The quantity of something produced.
(engineering, material science) yield strength of a material.
In the early part of growth or life; born not long ago.
definitions.example: a lamb is a young sheep

definitions.definition: At an early stage of existence or development; having recently come into existence.
definitions.example: the age of space travel is still young

definitions.definition: (Not) advanced in age; (far towards or) at a specified stage of existence or age.
definitions.example:
And thou, our Mother, twice two centuries young,
Bend with bright shafts of truth thy bow fresh-strung.

definitions.definition: (often as if a plural noun) Offspring, especially the immature offspring of animals.
definitions.example: The lion caught a gnu to feed its young.

definitions.definition: (informal or demography) To become or seem to become younger.
(informal or demography) To cause to appear younger.
(geology) To exhibit younging.
(uncountable) The quality or state of being young.
definitions.example: Feel awfully about Scott... It was a terrible thing for him to love youth so much that he jumped straight from youth to senility without going through manhood.…

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The part of life following childhood; the period of existence preceding maturity or age; the whole early part of life, from childhood, or, sometimes, from infancy, to adulthood.
definitions.example: Make the most of your youth, it will not last forever.

definitions.definition: (countable) A young person.
definitions.example: There was a group of youths hanging around the parking lot, reading fashion magazines and listening to music.

definitions.definition: Any of three species of subgenus Hippotigris: Equus grevyi, Equus quagga, or Equus zebra, all with black and white stripes and native to Africa.
(sports, slang) A referee.
(medicine, slang) An unlikely diagnosis, especially for symptoms probably caused by a common ailment.
Having a piquant or pungent taste; spicy.
Zestful.
(informal, LGBTQ) (of a man) Flamboyantly or effeminately gay.
Divided into zones.
Related to, associated with, or similar to zones.
(of air or ocean currents) roughly longitudinal (east to west, or west to east)
